q: During a year, the noting and drafting done in Hindi by an employee totals 11,000 words, and he seeks a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, as the minimum prescribed is 25,000 words in a year
options.B: He is not eligible, as the minimum prescribed is 50,000 words in a year
options.C: He is eligible only if the noting was done in a notified office
options.D: He is eligible for consideration, having done noting and drafting in Hindi of more than the prescribed minimum of 10,000 words in a year

e: The incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi prescribes a minimum of 10,000 words in a year; 11,000 words therefore makes the employee eligible for consideration.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 4,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.B: He is eligible, as the prescribed minimum is only 1,000 words in a year
options.C: He is eligible, as no minimum number of words is prescribed
options.D: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination in the same year

e: Consideration under the noting and drafting incentive scheme requires at least 10,000 words in Hindi in a year, so 4,000 words falls short and the employee is not eligible.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the third month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The personal pay is admissible only for the first month after the grant
options.B: The personal pay continues to be admissible, it being admissible for a period of twelve months
options.C: The personal pay ceases after two months from the grant
options.D: The personal pay is admissible only if the examination is passed again within that month

e: Personal pay equal to one increment granted on passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for twelve months, so it continues in the third month after grant.

q: A Central Government office spends 58 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books. With reference to the Annual Programme target for purchase of Hindi books for office libraries, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, as the prescribed proportion is 75 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short, as Hindi books must account for the entire amount
options.C: The office has complied, the prescribed proportion being at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books
options.D: No proportion for Hindi books is prescribed under the Annual Programme

e: The Annual Programme target is that at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on books for office libraries be spent on Hindi books; 58 per cent therefore complies.

q: A town has twenty Central Government offices located in it. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town, the correct position is:

options.A: No committee is required, the offices being too many to be coordinated
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted only in towns having fifty or more offices
options.C: Each office must implement the policy entirely on its own, without any town-level body
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the town having ten or more Central Government offices

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town having ten or more Central Government offices, so a town with twenty offices must have one.

q: A Central Government office renews a licence earlier issued by it and issues the renewal in English only, the dealing clerk contending that a renewal is not a fresh licence. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is:

options.A: A licence, including its renewal, is required to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.B: Only the original licence need be bilingual; a renewal may be in English only
options.C: A licence is required to be issued in Hindi only
options.D: Licences are outside the documents specified in Section 3(3)

e: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 requires specified documents, including a licence and its renewal, to be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office has to send an official communication to a member of the public residing in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be in:

options.A: Hindi, accompanied by its regional language translation
options.D: The regional language of the State in which he resides

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications to a member of the public in Region C are to be in English.

q: Two Central Government offices, both situated in Region 'B' and neither of them being a Ministry or Department or its attached or subordinate office, have to correspond with each other on an official matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such communications may be in:

options.A: The regional language of the State only

e: Communications between Central Government offices in Region B, other than Ministries, Departments and their attached or subordinate offices, may be in Hindi or English.

q: A State Government office located in Region 'C' has to correspond with a Central Government office on an official matter. Ordinarily, such correspondence from the State Government office to the Central Government office shall be in:

options.B: Hindi accompanied by an English translation
options.C: The regional language of the State

e: Correspondence from a State Government office in Region C to a Central Government office is ordinarily in English under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: An employee has passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as one of the subjects and claims that he possesses proficiency in Hindi. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: He shall be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi only, and not proficiency in Hindi, having passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as one of the subjects
options.B: Proficiency requires a degree in Hindi literature
options.C: He can be deemed proficient only after passing the Parangat examination
options.D: Residence in Region 'A' for ten years alone confers proficiency

e: Passing Matriculation with Hindi as a subject confers only working knowledge of Hindi under the Rules; proficiency requires Hindi as the medium or an equivalent higher standard.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
2. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 5 deems the Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance published under the President's authority to be its authoritative Hindi text; statement 2 does not correctly state Section 6.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(2) of the Constitution, the use of Hindi or any other language used for official purposes of a State, in the proceedings of a High Court having its principal seat in that State, may be authorised by the Governor of the State with the previous consent of the President.
2. Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court may be authorised by the Chief Justice of the High Court on his own.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 348(2) permits the Governor, with the President's previous consent, to authorise Hindi in High Court proceedings; Section 7 authorisation is not by the Chief Justice on his own.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Implementation Committee constituted in a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office.
2. Meetings of the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office are normally held every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The office Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the head of the office and normally meets every quarter to review Hindi implementation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau is mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices.
2. Besides such translation work, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Translation Bureau translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material and also runs translation training programmes for Central Government translators.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. The Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the Union Home Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the highest policy-making body for Hindi, chaired by the Prime Minister, with the Union Home Minister as its Vice-Chairman.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 345 of the Constitution, the Legislature of a State may by law adopt one or more of the languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language or languages of that State.
2. Under Article 346 of the Constitution, the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another, shall be the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 345 empowers a State Legislature to adopt a language in use in the State or Hindi as its official language, and Article 346 prescribes the Union language for Union-State communication.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, every person is entitled to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.
2. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, the endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups rests on the Central Government alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a grievance representation in any language used in the Union or the State; Article 350A places the endeavour on every State and local authority, not the Centre alone.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 have been framed by the Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 were framed under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and extend to the whole of India except Tamil Nadu.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
2. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 351 directs that Hindi draw its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, assimilating forms and expressions of Hindustani and Eighth Schedule languages without interfering with its genius.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of 30 members, of whom 20 are from the Lok Sabha and 10 are from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language has 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.

q: A Hindi version of a departmental circular is being prepared for issue to all field units. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Circular" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Circular in official glossaries is Paripatra.

q: A pay fixation note in Hindi has to record the yearly increase in pay of an employee. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Increment" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Increment, meaning the periodic yearly increase in pay, is Vetan Vriddhi.

q: An accounts clerk preparing the Hindi text of a correction slip issued to a pay bill has to write the term for a correction document. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Corrigendum" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Corrigendum, a document correcting errors, is Shuddhi Patra.

q: A leave account is being rendered in Hindi for an employee who has availed leave earned by him. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Earned Leave" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Earned Leave, leave earned by service, is Arjit Avakash.

q: A Hindi noting records the elevation of an employee to a higher post. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Promotion" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Promotion, elevation to a higher post, is Padonnati.

q: A disciplinary order is being issued in Hindi against an employee removed from service as a penalty. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dismissal" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Dismissal, removal from service as a penalty, is Barkhastagi.

q: A retirement dues statement is being prepared in Hindi for a superannuating employee. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Gratuity" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Gratuity, the retirement benefit paid on superannuation, is Upadan.

q: An office order in Hindi records that an officer has been sent to serve in another office for a temporary period. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Deputation" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Deputation, temporary service in another office, is Pratiniyukti.

q: A tour programme is being rendered in Hindi, showing the allowance admissible for journeys on duty. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Travelling Allowance" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Travelling Allowance for journeys on duty is Yatra Bhatta.

q: A litigant files a formal written request before a court, and its Hindi rendering is required in the case file. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Petition" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Petition, a formal written request before a court, is Yachika.

q: A training module on Article 344 of the Constitution asks trainees to identify the subject on which the Official Language Commission is required to make recommendations to the President. The correct subject is:

options.A: The translation of State Acts into the regional languages
options.B: The progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, restrictions on the use of English, the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the form of numerals to be used
options.C: The recognition of classical languages by the Government of India
options.D: The recruitment of Hindi Translators in Central Government offices

e: Under Article 344, the Official Language Commission recommends on the progressive use of Hindi, restrictions on English, language of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and the form of numerals.

q: While finalising its recommendations under Article 344 of the Constitution, an Official Language Commission is required to have due regard to:

options.A: The views expressed by the Kendriya Hindi Samiti alone
options.B: The financial resources available with the Union Government alone
options.C: The recommendations of the previous Commission alone
options.D: The industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services

e: Article 344 requires the Commission to have due regard to India's industrial, cultural and scientific advancement and the just claims and interests of non-Hindi speaking persons in public services.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify.
2. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, it is the duty of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 347 allows Presidential direction recognising a language spoken by a substantial proportion of a State's population, and Article 350B makes the Special Officer investigate safeguards for linguistic minorities.

q: A State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, and Acts passed by, that Legislature. An English translation of such a Bill, published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State, shall be deemed to be:

options.A: The authoritative text thereof in the English language
options.B: A mere unofficial summary for public information
options.C: Valid only within the districts of that State
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

e: Under Article 348(3), the English translation of a State Bill or Act published under the Governor's authority in the Official Gazette is deemed its authoritative text in English.

q: Where the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court has been authorised under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, every such judgment, decree or order is required to be accompanied by:

options.A: A summary of the judgment in the regional language of the State
options.B: A translation thereof in the English language issued under the authority of the High Court
options.C: A certificate of the Registrar of the High Court
options.D: A Hindi translation of the English text

e: Section 7 of the Official Languages Act requires every High Court judgment, decree or order in Hindi to be accompanied by an English translation issued under the High Court's authority.

q: The Governor of a State, with the previous consent of the President, authorises the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court of that State under Article 348(2) of the Constitution. An advocate claims that the authorisation also covers the judgments of that High Court. The correct position is that the authorisation does NOT extend to:

options.A: The arguments of the advocates in the Court
options.B: The pleadings filed in the Court
options.C: The day-to-day proceedings of the Court
options.D: Any judgment, decree or order passed or made by the High Court

e: The proviso to Article 348(2) expressly excludes any judgment, decree or order of the High Court from an authorisation covering its proceedings.

q: A reference note on Article 120(2) of the Constitution records the condition on which the use of English for the transaction of business in Parliament could continue beyond the initial period laid down in the Constitution. That condition is:

options.A: The President by order otherwise provides
options.B: The Official Language Commission recommends otherwise

e: Article 120(2) allowed English for Parliament's business beyond the initial period only if Parliament by law otherwise provides.

q: Under the proviso to Article 210(2) of the Constitution, in relation to the Legislatures of the States of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, the period for the continued use of English in the State Legislature was substituted by a period of:
e: The proviso to Article 210(2) substituted twenty-five years for fifteen years for the Legislatures of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

q: A newly constituted Committee of Parliament on Official Language asks which office provides its secretariat. The correct answer is:

options.D: The Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language.

q: After the Committee of Parliament on Official Language submits its report to the President under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the President shall cause the report to be:

options.A: Published in the Gazette of India only
options.B: Sent to the Supreme Court for its opinion
options.C: Considered by the Kendriya Hindi Samiti only
options.D: Laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all the State Governments

e: Under Section 4, after the Committee reports to the President, he causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all State Governments.

q: A member of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language proposes that its Chairman should be nominated by the President. The correct position regarding the Chairman of the Committee is that he is:

options.A: The Union Home Minister, ex officio
options.B: The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha on the Committee
options.C: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.D: Nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.

q: A translation unit of a Central Government office is advised to route its non-statutory translation work through the Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau). The Bureau functions as a subordinate office of the:

options.A: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
options.C: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The Central Translation Bureau functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: An accounts office addresses a query about the administrative control of the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra. The Institute functions under the:

options.A: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs

e: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra functions under the Ministry of Education, not the Department of Official Language.

q: A compendium on Hindi training records the year in which the Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced. The year recorded is:
e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme for in-service Hindi training of Central Government employees was introduced in 1955.

q: A probationer asks whether an employee nominated for Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme has to pay a fee and attend the classes after office hours. The correct position is that the training is:

options.A: Imparted on payment of a fee by the employee, outside office hours
options.C: Free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty
options.D: Imparted only while the employee is on casual leave

e: Training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is free of cost and imparted during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty.

q: An employee passes the prescribed Hindi examination entirely through his own efforts, without undergoing the prescribed training, and claims the incentive admissible for such a case. The incentive admissible to him is:

options.B: Out-of-turn promotion to the next grade
options.D: Free railway passes for the whole family

e: An employee who passes the prescribed Hindi examination through his own efforts, without undergoing the prescribed training, is entitled to a lumpsum award.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, meant for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
2. The Parangat course, meant for employees who have passed Pragya and require advanced proficiency in Hindi, is conducted through correspondence by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses and also the advanced Parangat course through correspondence.

q: A divisional office organises a Hindi workshop (Hindi Karyashala) for its dealing staff. The primary purpose of such a workshop is to:

options.A: Teach Hindi literature to the staff
options.B: Prepare the staff only for the Pragya examination
options.C: Celebrate Hindi Diwas in the office
options.D: Give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi

e: A Hindi workshop gives employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi, removing hesitation in its use.

q: An employee claims a cash award under the Department of Official Language's incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi merely on the ground that he disposed of the largest number of files in his section during the year. His claim is to be assessed mainly on the basis of:

options.A: His marks in the Pragya examination
options.B: The length of his service in Region 'A'
options.C: The number of words of noting and drafting written by him in Hindi during the year
options.D: The number of files disposed of by him in a year

e: The cash award for original noting and drafting in Hindi is assessed mainly on the number of words of noting and drafting written in Hindi during the year, not on files disposed of.

q: A town has several Central Government offices and a Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is constituted there. The Committee is chaired by:

options.A: The senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose
options.B: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.C: The District Magistrate of the district
options.D: The Hindi Officer of the biggest office in the town

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer, the head of office in the town, nominated for the purpose.

q: A note on the composition of the Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry records who, besides official members, are included in the Samiti. The correct record is:

options.B: Members of Parliament and non-official members nominated from among Hindi scholars and experts
options.D: Only officers of the Department of Official Language

e: A Ministry's Hindi Salahakar Samiti includes, besides official members, Members of Parliament and non-official members nominated from among Hindi scholars and experts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was first constituted in the year 1973.
2. The first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was Lalit Narayan Mishra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was first constituted in 1973, and its first Chairman was Lalit Narayan Mishra.

q: At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, a meeting of the Official Language Implementation Committee is convened to review the quarterly progress of Hindi work. The officer who presides over that meeting is the:
e: At a Zonal Railway headquarters, the Official Language Implementation Committee meeting is presided over by the General Manager.

q: Which of the following pairs relating to Official Language Implementation Committees is correctly matched?

options.A: Divisional Official Language Implementation Committee of a Railway Division — the General Manager of the Zonal Railway
options.B: Central Official Language Implementation Committee — the Union Home Minister
options.C: Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office — the Hindi Translator of the office
options.D: Town Official Language Implementation Committee — the senior-most Central Government officer in the town, nominated for the purpose

e: The Town Official Language Implementation Committee is correctly paired with the senior-most Central Government officer in the town, nominated for the purpose, as its chairman.

q: A model station and a model workshop of a Zonal Railway put in claims for Rajbhasha recognition on the ground that, apart from Zonal Railways and Divisions, such recognition on Indian Railways also extends to:

options.B: Hindi authors employed in the Railways

e: Besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, Rajbhasha recognition on Indian Railways extends to Adarsh, or model, stations and Adarsh workshops.

q: In a region-identification exercise for newly posted assistants, one of the following pairs (Union Territory/State — Region under the Official Language Rules, 1976) is correctly matched. Identify it:
e: Puducherry is placed in Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976, whereas Haryana is in Region A, Maharashtra in Region B and Assam in Region C.

q: A Central Government office has to send an official communication to a State Government office located at Ahmedabad in Gujarat, a State placed in Region 'B'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such a communication shall ordinarily be in:

options.B: The regional language of the State
options.C: English, accompanied by a summary in the regional language

e: Communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region B, such as Gujarat, shall ordinarily be in Hindi under the Rules.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in Hindi to an office located at Thiruvananthapuram in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication must be accompanied by:

options.B: A covering letter in the regional language of that State
options.C: A Hindi summary of the communication
options.D: A certificate of the head of the issuing office

e: A communication in Hindi sent to an office in Region C must be accompanied by its English translation under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: Punjab and Haryana enter into an agreement that a particular language shall be the official language for communication between the two States. Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, the language covered by such an agreement is:

options.C: The regional language of either State

e: The proviso to Article 346 provides that where two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the language for communication between them, Hindi may be used for that purpose.

q: A provision of Article 343(3) of the Constitution is cited in a note on numerals. The Article empowers Parliament to provide by law, for the purposes specified therein, for the use of:

options.B: The numerals of the regional languages

e: Article 343(3) empowers Parliament to provide by law for the use of the Devanagari form of numerals for the purposes specified therein.

q: In a quiz on the constitutional provisions relating to language, candidates are asked in which Articles of the Constitution the Eighth Schedule is referred to. The correct answer is:
e: The Eighth Schedule is referred to in Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution, relating to the Official Language Commission and the development of Hindi.

q: A note on the development of Hindi under Article 351 of the Constitution records the sources from which Hindi is to be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating forms, style and expressions. Those sources are:

options.A: Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule

e: Article 351 directs Hindi to be enriched by assimilating forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule.

q: A citizen wishes to submit a representation for the redress of a grievance to an authority of a State. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, he is entitled to submit the representation in:

options.B: Any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be
options.D: Only the official language of the State concerned

e: Article 350 entitles a citizen to submit a grievance representation in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, the President may issue such directions to any State as he considers necessary or proper for securing the provision of facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
2. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submits his reports on the working of the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 350A empowers the President to issue directions to a State for mother-tongue instruction facilities, and under Article 350B the Special Officer reports to the President.

q: The Union has to communicate with a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the language to be used for such communication is:

options.B: The regional language of the State

e: Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act provides that communication between the Union and a State that has not adopted Hindi as its official language shall be in English.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a member of the public residing at Lucknow in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the region
options.D: Hindi or English, at the choice of the officer issuing it

e: Under the Official Language Rules, communications to a member of the public in Region A, such as at Lucknow, shall be in Hindi.

q: A planning note asks how often the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, containing the targets to be achieved by Central Government offices, is issued by the Department of Official Language. It is issued:

options.D: Only when the Committee of Parliament on Official Language so recommends

e: The Annual Programme containing targets for the progressive use of Hindi by Central Government offices is issued by the Department of Official Language every year.

q: An office finalises its Quarterly Progress Report (Traimasik Pragati Report) on the progressive use of Hindi. The report is submitted by the office to:

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language, directly
options.C: Its controlling office / administrative Ministry or Department

e: An office submits its Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi to its controlling office or administrative Ministry or Department.

q: A dealing assistant assumes that the Official Language Policy is implemented through compulsion and penal action against employees who do not know Hindi. The correct position is that the policy is implemented mainly through:

options.A: Stoppage of increments of employees who do not pass Pragya
options.B: Making Hindi the sole medium of all office work from a fixed date
options.C: Transfer of non-Hindi knowing staff to Region 'C'
options.D: Persuasion, encouragement and incentives, and not through compulsion

e: The Official Language Policy is implemented mainly through persuasion, encouragement and incentives, and not through compulsion or penal action.

q: A note explaining the regional classification under the Official Language Rules records the basis on which States are placed in Region 'A', Region 'B' or Region 'C'. That basis is mainly:

options.A: The extent to which Hindi is the official language of the State and is widely spoken and understood there
options.B: The geographical size of the State
options.C: The number of Central Government offices located in the State
options.D: The literacy rate of the State

e: States are placed in Regions A, B or C mainly according to the extent to which Hindi is the official language of the State and is widely spoken and understood there.

q: Besides the State of Uttarakhand, Sanskrit has also been declared as the second official language of the State of:
e: Besides Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh has also declared Sanskrit as its second official language.

q: An employee who cannot attend regular training classes enrols for a Hindi course by correspondence, while his office separately arranges in-service Hindi training for its staff during office hours. The correspondence course and the in-service training are the respective responsibilities of:

options.A: The Central Hindi Training Institute and the Central Hindi Directorate
options.B: The Central Hindi Directorate and the Central Translation Bureau
options.C: The Central Hindi Directorate and the Central Hindi Training Institute
options.D: The Central Translation Bureau and the Central Hindi Directorate

e: Hindi correspondence courses are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate, while in-service Hindi training is the responsibility of the Central Hindi Training Institute.

q: A note on the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, records its Vice-Chairman. The Vice-Chairman of the Samiti is the:
e: The Vice-Chairman of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the Union Home Minister.

q: The World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya), set up for the promotion of Hindi at the international level, has its headquarters in:
e: The World Hindi Secretariat, set up to promote Hindi internationally, has its headquarters in Mauritius.

q: A Rajbhasha calendar of historical events records the year in which Hindi Diwas, observed on 14th September, was celebrated for the first time. The year recorded is:
e: Hindi Diwas, observed on 14 September to mark the adoption of Hindi in 1949, was celebrated for the first time in 1953.

q: To stop bilingual documents from leaving a Central Government office in English alone, the office earmarks its despatch section for checking every outgoing bilingual document. Such earmarked points are known as:
e: Points earmarked in an office, including the despatch section, to check that bilingual documents do not go out in English alone are known as Check Points.

q: A dealing assistant records a noting in Hindi. His officer, instead of returning the file, insists that the assistant himself must also supply an English rendering of that noting. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976:

options.A: The assistant must supply the rendering whenever the officer asks for it
options.B: The assistant cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting in the other language
options.C: Only a gazetted officer can be asked to supply such a rendering
options.D: The rendering must be bought from an outside translator at the assistant's cost

e: Under the Official Language Rules, an employee who does noting or drafting in Hindi cannot be required to furnish a translation of it in the other language.

q: A Central Government office has to write to a foreign embassy located in India on an official matter. The correspondence is to be conducted in:

options.C: Hindi and English together, as with bilingual documents
options.D: The official language of the country the embassy represents

e: Correspondence with a foreign embassy located in India on official matters is conducted in English.

q: A passenger rings up the complaint cell of a railway office and puts his grievance in Hindi. The official who picks up the call should, as far as possible, answer him:

options.A: In English only, telephone replies being official communications
options.B: Only after passing the call to the Hindi Cell
options.C: In the regional language of the place where the office sits

e: A grievance put on telephone in Hindi should, as far as possible, be answered in Hindi by the official receiving the call.

q: An office is buying a software package for its day-to-day work and the purchase committee wants the package to support office work in Hindi as well. Such packages are required to have:

options.A: English-only working, Hindi work being left to typewriters
options.C: Working only in the regional language of the State of posting
options.D: Hindi-only working, with no provision for English at all

e: Software packages bought for day-to-day office work are required to have bilingual, Hindi-English, working capability.

q: The information technology section of an office is standardising the keyboard to be used for Hindi typing on its computers. The standard layout prescribed for the purpose, as per the Bureau of Indian Standards standard adopted for it, is:

options.B: A phonetic layout designed by each office for itself
options.D: The English QWERTY layout with stickers pasted on the keys

e: The standard keyboard layout prescribed for Hindi typing on computers, as per the Bureau of Indian Standards standard, is InScript.

q: An office prepares its Hindi documents on computers and wants them readable and exchangeable on any other computer system. The font and encoding it should use for Hindi work is:

options.A: A Unicode-compliant font such as Mangal
options.B: The Kruti Dev font, which is system-specific
options.C: Any ornamental English font with Hindi characters pasted as pictures
options.D: Handwritten text scanned and pasted into the document

e: Hindi documents should use a Unicode-compliant font such as Mangal so that they are readable and exchangeable on any computer system.

q: A Zonal Railway is launching a new public portal and proposes to keep it in English alone for speed of launch. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained:

options.D: In Hindi and English, in bilingual form

e: Websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in bilingual form, in Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office is releasing a recruitment advertisement and proposes to place it only in English newspapers. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the advertisement should be released:

options.A: In Hindi and English newspapers, in bilingual form
options.B: In English newspapers only, advertisements being meant for the educated public
options.C: Only in the regional language newspaper of the area
options.D: Only in Hindi newspapers during Hindi Pakhwada and in English newspapers otherwise

e: Recruitment advertisements should be released in Hindi and English newspapers in bilingual form under the Official Language Policy.

q: A newly opened stores depot gets its rubber stamps made in English alone, treating stamps as internal stationery. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, rubber stamps used in an office should be prepared:

options.C: In bilingual form, in Hindi and English

e: Rubber stamps used in an office should be prepared in bilingual form, in Hindi and English, under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions.

q: The establishment branch of an office gets the headings of its registers printed in English alone. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the headings of registers used in Central Government offices are required to be printed:

options.D: In Hindi and English, in bilingual form

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, headings of registers used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English, in bilingual form.

q: A printing order for the letter-heads of a Central Government office is placed with the text in English alone. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, letter-heads used in such offices are required to be printed:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English.

q: An accounts office is reprinting its codes, manuals, forms and other procedural literature and proposes an English-only reprint. Such literature of Central Government offices is required to be printed and published:

options.B: In diglot form, in Hindi and English

e: Codes, manuals, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are required to be printed and published in diglot form, in Hindi and English.

q: At a railway reservation office, the requisition forms handed to passengers for reservation and cancellation are found printed in English alone. Such forms are required to be printed:

options.C: In Hindi and English, in bilingual form

e: Forms for reservation and cancellation handed to passengers are required to be printed in Hindi and English, in bilingual form.

q: A new station building is being fitted with name boards, designation boards and sign boards. The three languages on such boards are to appear in the order:
e: On name boards, designation boards and sign boards, the three languages appear in the order: regional language, Hindi, English.

q: The public address system at a railway station is being reprogrammed for passenger guidance. Announcements for the guidance of passengers at railway stations are made in:

options.A: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English
options.C: English and the regional language only

e: Announcements for the guidance of passengers at railway stations are made in three languages: the regional language, Hindi and English.

q: A citizen's grievance letter, written and sent in Hindi, reaches a Central Government office. The reply to that letter must be sent:

options.C: In the regional language of the State
options.D: In either Hindi or English, at the dealing clerk's discretion

e: A letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, regardless of the region in which the office is located.

q: A contract file shows that the agreement was signed and issued in English alone, and the lapse is traced to the officer who signed it. Under the Official Languages Act, 1963, the responsibility for ensuring that such bilingual documents are issued in both Hindi and English rests with:

options.B: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.C: The Head of the Office alone

e: Under the Official Languages Act, the responsibility for ensuring that a bilingual document is issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document.

q: During an inspection, a lapse in compliance with the Official Languages Act and the Rules is noticed in a Central Government office. Under Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the responsibility for ensuring proper compliance in the office rests with:

options.A: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.B: The Section Officer of the establishment branch
options.C: The administrative head of the office
options.D: The officer who signs the documents

e: Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976 places responsibility for ensuring proper compliance with the Act and Rules on the administrative head of the office.

q: An employee has passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as one of the subjects and claims to be treated accordingly under the Official Language Rules, 1976. He shall be deemed to possess:

options.A: Working knowledge of Hindi only, and nothing more
options.C: No recognised knowledge of Hindi until he passes Pragya
options.D: Proficiency in Hindi only if he was born in Region 'A'

e: Passing Matriculation with Hindi as one of the subjects deems an employee to possess working knowledge of Hindi only, not proficiency.

q: An employee who has not passed any Hindi examination states in writing that he is in possession of working knowledge of Hindi. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he shall also be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi if he:

options.A: Is a native of a Region 'A' State
options.B: Has studied Hindi as an optional subject in school
options.C: Declares himself to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Has been posted in Region 'A' for one year

e: An employee who declares himself in writing to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi is also deemed to have acquired working knowledge under the Rules.

q: An employee has passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as the medium of examination and seeks recognition of his Hindi knowledge. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he shall be deemed to possess:

options.C: No knowledge of Hindi until he passes Praveen
options.D: Working knowledge only after one year of service in Region 'A'

e: Passing Matriculation with Hindi as the medium of examination deems an employee to possess proficiency in Hindi under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: An office has been individually notified in the Official Gazette under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976. In such a notified office, an employee who has acquired working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting:

options.B: In the regional language of the State
options.C: In Hindi or in English, entirely at his own choice in all cases
options.D: In Hindi, on the subjects specified in the notification

e: In an office notified under Rule 10(4), an employee with working knowledge of Hindi can be required to do noting and drafting in Hindi on the subjects specified in the notification.

q: In an office that has not been so notified, an employee who possesses working knowledge of Hindi records his noting on a file. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he may make noting and drafting:

options.C: In Hindi or in English, as he may choose

e: In an office that is not notified, an employee with working knowledge of Hindi may do noting and drafting in Hindi or in English, as he may choose.

q: A Central Government office is writing to a State Government office located in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the communication shall be issued in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi accompanied by an English translation

e: Communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region C shall be issued in English under the Official Language Rules, 1976.
